sections.h2: Where is the Lawrence County recorder's office?
sections.html:
The Lawrence County Recorder is inside the Court House at 111 South 4th Street, Suite 21, in Ironton, OH 45638. The contact page lists a phone at 740-533-4314, a fax at 740-533-4411, a recorder@lawrencecountyohiorecorder.org email and weekday hours of 8 to 4. Ironton is the county seat and the county's largest city.

Think of the office as the county's permanent land file. Its common documents page names warranty and quit claim deeds, survivorship deeds, sheriff's deeds, certificates of transfer, affidavits of transfer, life estate terminations and transfer on death designation and confirmation affidavits. It also names mortgage releases and assignments, land contracts, plats, powers of attorney, zoning maps and a long run of liens, from mechanic's liens to federal tax liens and child support liens.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Lawrence County?
sections.html:
A fee notice on the recorder's site says that on January 1, 2025 most recording fees went up by $5.00, the preservation surcharge that Senate Bill 94 allowed. A one or two page document now runs $39.00 and every added page costs $8.00, so the printed chart climbs by $8 a page to $103.00 at ten pages. Half of what the office collects is sent to the state for the Ohio Housing Trust Fund, consistent with section 317.32.

The chart is footnoted: $4.00 reference fees and the standardization charge are extra. The recorder's fee is only one piece of closing, and the tax credits that appear on second half 2025 bills are another. Here are the credits the auditor printed, by school district.

sections.h2: How do you avoid the extra $20 charge at the Lawrence County recorder?
sections.html:
Prepare the deed to the layout in section 317.114, which covers documents prepared after June 30, 2009. Per the office's guideline page, a deed that misses it costs $20.00 more. Its checklist:

  • Computer type of at least 10 point.
  • Sheets between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Black or blue ink only, with no highlighter.
  • One inch of margin on both sides and the bottom of each page.
  • A 3 inch strip at the top of page one that only the recorder, auditor and engineer may use, then 1.5 inches at the top of later pages.

Court and taxing authority papers, plats, DD214 discharges, state or federal documents and older instruments fall outside the rule. A margin guidelines PDF on the site helps whoever drafts the deed.

sections.h2: What happens at the Lawrence County auditor before a deed reaches the recorder?
sections.html:
The auditor is at 111 S Fourth Street, phone (740) 533-4310, open weekdays 8 to 4. Under section 319.202, the buyer files a statement of value, the seller pays the conveyance fee and the auditor endorses the deed.

The state charge in section 319.54(G)(3) is $1 or ten cents per $100, whichever is more, and a county can add a transfer tax capped at thirty cents per $100 under section 322.02. Counties choose their own totals, so the quickest check is the Conveyance Fee Calculator in the Tools menu of the auditor's site, which includes the parcel transfer fee. Type in a parcel count and a sale price, and it returns a charge.

sections.h2: Which Lawrence County records can you search?
sections.html:
The recorder's home page sets out coverage. The current index runs from 1982 for deeds, 1988 for mortgages, 1989 for financing statements and 1981 for leases, liens and miscellaneous records. A second online index reaches much further back.

  • Deed grantor and grantee entries date from 1818 to 1984, and mortgages from 1834 to 1988.
  • Plats are listed from 1818 to 2010, and leases from 1864 to 1981.
  • Index books online include deed volumes 1 through 475 and mortgage volumes 82 through 441.
  • Odd corners of the archive include veterans grave plats and a soldiers discharge index covering 1864 to 1865.

Staff will help with a search during business hours. A title search that stops at the 1982 deed index can miss older easements, so ask where the older books begin for your parcel.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Lawrence County itself?
sections.html:
This is the southernmost county in Ohio, part of Appalachian Ohio and the Huntington-Ashland metropolitan area, with part of Wayne National Forest inside its lines. It touches Cabell and Wayne Counties in West Virginia and Boyd and Greenup Counties in Kentucky. Formed December 20, 1816 from parts of Gallia and Scioto, it moved its seat from Burlington to Ironton in 1851, and the present courthouse dates to 1908. County histories date the first settlers to Hanging Rock on the Ohio River in 1796.

Census QuickFacts for Lawrence County: 55,710 people in mid 2025, which is 4.3 percent fewer than in April 2020. Housing units, 26,564. Owner occupancy, 72.3 percent. Typical value of an owned home in 2020 to 2024, $144,000. Median gross rent, $848. Median household income, $58,325, with 15.0 percent of residents in poverty. Builders took out 23 permits in 2025.

sections.h2: How did House Bill 186 change second half 2025 bills in Lawrence County?
sections.html:
The auditor's home page says the Inflation Cap Credit appears on second half 2025 real estate bills, which were mailed July 9, 2026. It is based on new revenue each school district gained from the 20 mill floor measured against inflation, and it did not alter any appraised value. A buyer or title agent can view the credit by searching the parcel on the auditor's site.

An owner who paid before the credit was applied needs to do nothing, because any overpayment rolls into the 2026 first half bill. Ask the auditor how a carried credit should show on a closing statement.

sections.h2: Which tools does the Lawrence County auditor offer sellers?
sections.html: Beyond the calculator, the auditor's Tools menu holds a Tax Estimator, a Sales Report, a Sales List and a Delinquency Report. The sales reports list recent sales in the county, which helps when you set a price. The auditor's site also carries a GIS parcel viewer through its map link, and a search page that shows the appraisal and payment history for any parcel.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Lawrence County, Ohio?
faqs.a: At the Lawrence County Recorder, Court House, 111 South 4th Street, Suite 21, Ironton, OH 45638, phone 740-533-4314. Stop at the county auditor first so the statement of value and conveyance fee are handled.

faqs.q: How much does the Lawrence County recorder charge for a deed?
faqs.a: The fee notice shows $39.00 for one or two pages and $8.00 for each page after that, effective January 1, 2025. $4.00 reference fees and the $20.00 standardization charge apply when triggered.

faqs.q: Is there a way to estimate the Lawrence County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The auditor's website has a Conveyance Fee Calculator, with parcel count and sale price as inputs, and the page says it includes the parcel transfer fee. The auditor's office at (740) 533-4310 can confirm a figure.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed breaks the Ohio margin rules?
faqs.a: The recorder accepts it and adds $20.00. The 3 inch top margin on page one is reserved for the recorder, auditor and engineer. Court papers, plats, DD214s, state or federal documents and older instruments are exempt from the rule.

faqs.q: How far back do Lawrence County deed records run online?
faqs.a: The current index lists deeds from 1982 forward, and the older online index lists grantor and grantee entries from 1818 to 1984. Index books include deed volumes 1 through 475. Ask the recorder about anything the online index does not reach.
